title: The Polka-Dotted Car and the Shadow Lab
summary: Uncle Grisco is interrupted during his scientific experiments by his friend Victor, who needs a watering can for the flowers in his backyard playhouse. The pair sets off in a vibrant pink and blue striped car with orange polka dots to Mischief's Hardware Store. After a search through tiny dollhouse supplies, Victor finds a medium-sized red watering can with orange polka dots. Upon returning, they dive back into the wonders of science, exploring how the position of light creates shadows of vastly different sizes.

highlightQuote.text: Magnets make colors and finger puppets make shadows.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Ah, there we go. All right. Where do you want to be for Stars and Stories?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Over here first.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, that sounds nice. Okay.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Daddy, daddy.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Yes.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Dad, let's tell an Uncle Grisco story.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okay. Once upon a time, Uncle Grisco was in his house doing some experiments, when suddenly, what happened?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Ding-dong.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: "Oh, who's at my door?" says Uncle Grisco.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Victor.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: "Oh, hi, Victor. Welcome to my house. Um, what, uh, why, why did you come over today?"

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Because I s- have something interesting to do.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: "Oh? What have you got?"

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Uh, I had no watering can to water my beautiful pink flowers in the backyard of my playhouse.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: "Oh, you need a watering can?"

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: "Well-"

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: But there's no watering can at my house.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: "Oh, that's too bad."

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Can, can we go to the hardware store together?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: "Well, that's a good idea. I, I love going to the hardware store," said Uncle Grisco. "There's really good things there for doing experiments with, but also good things for gardening." So, Uncle Grisco and Victor got in Uncle Grisco's little car. What kind of little car did Uncle Grisco have?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: He had a pink and blue striped car with orange polka dots.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Wow, that sounds like an awesome little car. And vroom, vroom, vroom, vroom, vroom, they drove to the hardware store. And who is the owner of the hardware store?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Mischief.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Mischief Mouse said, "Oh, welcome Uncle Grisco and Victor. What can I help you with today-

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Um, we need a w-

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: ... at the Mischief Hardware Store?"

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Um, we need a watering can to water Victor's pink flowers in her backyard of her playhouse.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: "Well, that's a wonderful thing to come to my hardware store. And look, I've got a brand-new shipment of teeny-tiny dollhouse watering cans. You see this? You can carry 20 of them in your palm. Look, it's just big enough for a tiny drop of water. It's a perfect size for a dollhouse.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: How about that? Would you like one, or would you like a whole bunch?"

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I, I want a pink, I want a pink one with, uh, um, I want a pink one with yellow polka dots, said Mis- said, said Victor.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: "Oh, pink with yellow polka dots. I'm afraid none of these teeny-tiny dollhouse watering cans are, uh, of that color scheme. But why don't we look around in the back and see if we have anything else?"

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Well, then, well, actually, actually, Slicker and Slickerio bought that one. So, so what about we take an orange... So, or let's get a red one with orange polka dots.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, yeah, red with orange polka dots. I think I did see one of those on the shelf. Now, would you like a medium-sized watering can or a large watering can?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: A medium size.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, that sounds, sounds like a good choice. Okay, here you go. That will be 25 cents. Do you have 25 cents to pay for it?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Mm-hmm.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okay, there we go. Nice doing business with you. "Thank you," said Mischief Mouse. And so, uh, Uncle Grisco and Victor took their new watering can and got back in the car and went vroom, vroom, vroom, vroom, vroom. Now, did they go to Victor's house or Uncle Grisco's house?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Mm, and Victor watered his pink flowers and then went right back to Uncle Grisco's house.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh. And he said, "Well, Uncle Grisco, thanks for helping me with that. And now I can water my plants. But what kind of experiments were you doing?" And what did Uncle Grisco say?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I don't know.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, Uncle Grisco said, "I was experimenting with light and colors and shadows. Do you have any questions about those things?"

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Uh, yeah. Magnets make colors, and finger puppets make shadows.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, you mean Magna-Tiles. "Yes, I love those," said Uncle Grisco.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: And-

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: "I've got a whole set right here."

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah, and also finger puppets make shadows.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, yes, like shadow puppets. That's fun. I love doing that. But what do you wonder about those things? What would you like to know?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Well, let's just keep telling the story, then you'll find out.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh. "Well," Uncle Grisco said, "have you ever noticed that sometimes shadows are really big, and sometimes they're really small? Have you noticed that?"

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Now, how do you make a shadow that's really big?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I don't know.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Well, we'll have to experiment with it to- together sometime, because it's fun to play around with. If you put the light and the thing you're making the shadow with close together, and there's a wall or some other surface to project the shadow onto that's far away, that will make the shadow really big.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: But if the light is far away and the thing casting the shadow is close to the wall, then the shadow will be small.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Hmm.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: And have you ever noticed when you're walking down the sidewalk, if the sun is low in the sky, like very early in the day or very late when the sun is setting, sometimes you have a very long shadow. Has that ever happened to you?

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: No, it never happened to me.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh. Well, look out for that, because it's an interesting thing, and you can think about why it happens, too. Oh, and that's our light blinking. So I think that's all the time we've got for Stars and Stories.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah, that's all the time we've got.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okie-dokey.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Dad, I'm great at turning on the lamp, so don't turn it on.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Okay.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: I'll, I'll turn it on.

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: Oh, thanks.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: See how I was a great lamp turner-on?

transcript.speaker: Dad
transcript.text: I did see that.

transcript.speaker: Izzy
transcript.text: Yeah

characters.name: Uncle Grisco
characters.description: A nomadic mole scientist and science teacher, this subterranean inventor resides in a home brimming with wondrous experiments, serving as a devoted confidant to the gopher folk. Within his laboratory of glowing elixirs and prismatic shadows, he fuses volcanic lore with the study of light to translate the planet's restless movements and the scarred history of cosmic craters. A wandering sage who maps both deep tectonic veins and celestial paths, he frequently emerges from his sprawling tunnels to share ancient botanical secrets and astronomical insights with his friend Seeker.

characters.name: Victor
characters.description: Clad in blue shorts and a purple shirt, Lily’s brother is a tiny baby mouse and spirited cosmic stowaway who once served as a royal gardener within the Magic Forest’s glitter-shimmering houses. Now a rugged driver of a tow truck in the big car race, he balances his mechanical duties with a quest for a celestial watering can and the composition of percussive ‘bamp-bam-bum’ beats for space-faring worms. Though he treasures the sparkly art of Uncle Grisco and Hattie, his high-speed adventures often result in muddy messes that necessitate restorative baths, leaving him in singular pursuit of the perfect hat to complete his interstellar ensemble.

characters.name: Mischief Mouse
characters.description: Reigning from a purple-striped Jovian castle, this affable mouse King—a playful-named companion to Pinecone Mouse—is a seasoned adventurer, guardian of the Underground Library, and Hattie’s steadfast ally. Between savoring artisanal cheeses and awaiting a rugged cardboard replacement for his fragile Lego hat, he spends leisure hours meticulously constructing and gleefully smashing soaring towers. A pancake-loving monarch who once tended shop for mountain-dwelling traffic cones, his cosmic quests recently shifted from the stars to the speedway; having borrowed a tow truck from Mistress Mouse, he proved a formidable competitor who nearly clinched a stunning victory. Whether piloting starships or joining the group’s latest trek to Nana’s house, he remains a vigilant protector and devoted friend across the galaxy.

places.name: Uncle Grisco's House
places.description: Uncle Grisco’s subterranean home is a sprawling burrow and sophisticated laboratory where local moles frequently congregate. Within these earthen walls, cozy domesticity meets the hum of progress, as tangled roots frame glowing vials and intricate machinery dedicated to clandestine experiments and scientific discovery.
